transcript.answer: At most 3 implementation-loop upkeep runs can start per repository for a single push to main (or completed check suite). Each run starts the implementation-loop at the sync-pr entry. When more than 3 settled loop pull requests need upkeep, the pull requests that have never had an upkeep run go first. The cap then takes the 3 oldest pull requests. I did not find how the two rules combine when there are ties. The tool results don't spell it out. The rest wait for a later event. A pull request only qualifies if GitHub marks it behind main, conflicted, or red on CI, and its ticket must not be parked with lore:blocked.

judgements.reason: The answer correctly gives the cap of 3 per event per repository and puts never-upkept pull requests first, but it omits the key rule that the pull request whose newest upkeep run started earliest goes next, and it hedges about how the ordering combines.
